title: Scan the container image against vulnerabilities
description: Scan OS packages and application dependencies in built, stored, and deployed image digests, and rescan as vulnerability intelligence changes. Assign remediation owners and deadlines and rebuild affected images. Scanning identifies known issues; a clean result is not proof that an image is secure.

title: Allow deploying containers only from known registries
description: Enforce approved registry and repository paths with admission policy, including init and ephemeral containers. Restrict who can push or import into those repositories and combine source allowlists with digest and signature verification. Egress filtering is defense in depth, not a substitute for admission enforcement because cached images can run without a pull.

Enforce supported admission policies with Azure Policy for AKS
Using egress lockdown and authorizing only the URL of your registry

title: Block promotion and redeployment of images with newly discovered issues
description: Continuously reassess image digests after publication and block promotion or new deployment when they violate policy. Use a supported admission and registry-access workflow rather than assuming a registry scan automatically quarantines images.
detail: Track affected running workloads and cached images, rebuild and redeploy fixed digests, and document emergency exceptions. Blocking new image pulls does not stop existing containers or prevent cached images from being reused; coordinate containment with incident response.

title: Use least-privilege identity-based access to container registries
description: Use separate identities for image publishing and pulling; disable the ACR admin account unless explicitly required. Grant the AKS kubelet managed identity pull-only permissions, not the application workload identity. Use AcrPull for registry RBAC mode; ABAC-enabled registries require Container Registry Repository Reader and do not support az aks --attach-acr. Scope repository permissions where supported.

title: Enforce the required container registry network access boundary
applicability: Applies when the registry threat model or network policy requires private connectivity or restricted public endpoints; private endpoint adoption alone is not a readiness requirement.
description: Enforce the registry access boundary required by the threat model. For private access, use ACR Premium Private Link, configure private DNS and connectivity to registry and regional data endpoints, and disable public network access after validation. If private connectivity is not required, select an appropriate SKU with explicitly authorized public access rather than requiring Premium solely to pass this check.
detail: Test image pulls from every node pool and DR region, plus CI builds and imports. Verify permitted and denied paths and that no public bypass remains where public access is prohibited. A private endpoint alone neither disables public access nor replaces identity-based authorization.

title: Use minimal, maintained runtime images
description: Use a supported minimal or distroless runtime image appropriate for the application, architecture, and OS. Remove build tools and unused packages, run as non-root, and rebuild regularly from maintained bases.
detail: Distroless images reduce attack surface but do not prevent exploitation or container escape. Validate certificates, runtime dependencies, patch availability, and a controlled debugging workflow rather than adding a shell to the production image.

title: Refresh container when base image is updated
description: Track base-image and dependency updates, including digest-pinned bases, and automate rebuilds followed by tests, scanning, signing, and staged redeployment. Updating a base image or rebuilding an application does not patch already-running containers; promote and deploy the new digest and retain a tested rollback image.

title: Sign OCI artifacts and verify trusted publishers before deployment
description: Sign released image digests and other OCI artifacts using supported tooling such as Notation. Verify integrity and trusted publisher identity in build and deployment workflows, and enforce verification at admission where supported. Define trust policies, certificate rotation, revocation response, and narrowly scoped exceptions; merely storing a signature in ACR does not enforce trust.

title: Retain SBOMs and build provenance linked to immutable image digests
description: Generate software bills of materials and build provenance for releases, associate them with the exact OCI image digest, and retain them with signatures and scan evidence. Record source revision, builder identity, and dependencies for incident investigation. Protect build identities and verify evidence before promotion; an SBOM alone does not establish image integrity or absence of vulnerabilities.
